title: fix(plugin-list): a list view whose every column is FLS-denied still sends a `$select` (#10275)
body:
Fixes #10275

## What changed

`ListView`'s `$select` builder (`selectFields` in `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx`) drops the authored columns the principal cannot read. When that left no column it returned `undefined`, so the request carried **no `$select` key** and asked for every field, the denied ones included.

The builder now asks whether the author declared any column (`rawCols.length === 0`), before the FLS filter, not whether any column survived it. That is the rule `hasAuthoredColumns` already applies to what the grid draws. An authored list that FLS empties now falls through to the existing union: `id` plus the `$expand` roots, the view bindings, the grid's grouping fields and the row predicates' operands. Each of these is already FLS-gated as it enters (the platform columns excepted, as `addSpeculative` documents). That is the shape `ObjectGrid` (`ensureId([])` keeps `['id']`) and `RelatedList` (PR objectui#10258) send.

No new helper: the predicate harvest `RelatedList` uses (core's `listViewPredicates` + `collectPredicateFieldRefs` + `PLATFORM_RECORD_COLUMNS`) is the one this builder already calls. The fix moves one early return and adds a comment. The harvest itself is untouched (objectui#10277 is a separate card).

Unchanged, and pinned as controls:
- no authored `columns` (absent or `[]`) still sends no `$select`;
- a partially-denied list (`[subject, salary]`, `salary` denied) still sends `['id', 'subject']`;
- before the permission answer loads, nothing is filtered.

One deliberate widening of the triage wording ("`id` plus the row predicates' fields"): the view bindings, grouping fields and `$expand` roots are kept too. They are per-row reads, each already FLS-gated. Dropping them would empty a kanban lane or a calendar date on an all-denied list. A readable binding is kept and a denied one is dropped; both are pinned.

## Tests

New `packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListView.allDeniedSelect-10275.test.tsx` (7 cases), using the same `usePermissions` stub as `ListView.speculativeFls-7216.test.tsx`:
- `[salary, industry]` both denied: `$select` is present and equals `['id']`;
- all columns denied, plus conditional formatting on `status` and a declared action with `visible` on `region` and `disabled` on `priority`: `$select` sorted is `['id', 'region', 'status']`, and the denied `priority` is not added back;
- a readable kanban `groupByField` is kept and a denied one is dropped;
- controls: partially denied, no authored columns (absent and `[]`), policy not loaded;
- the policy answering late re-projects the request to `['id']`.

Ablation (after committing the fix; `ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode with its own restore): the anchor `if (rawCols.length === 0) return undefined;` was replaced by the old survivor test. The mutation landed (anchor 1 to 0, blob `91d6ab5662` to `4ce7fc7d2a`). Result: **4 failed / 3 passed**. The 4 failures are the finding pins; the 3 passes are the controls. Restore was proven: blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty. The first attempt's replacement contained the anchor, so the tool refused it before running anything (a no-op, and restored). It is reported here, not counted.

At head `11962d420`:
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-list/`: **85 files / 1029 tests passed**;
- plugin-list `type-check` (both `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`; the new test is in that program per `--listFilesOnly`) exited 0, after the dependency closure build (`turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/plugin-list^...`, 12/12 cached);
- eslint on the two touched source files: 0 errors (JSON output, 2 files). Type-aware linting is not enabled in `eslint.config.js` and no local rule reads the disk, so this diff cannot move the verdict of any untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI;
- these all exited 0: `check-changeset-presence`, `-no-major`, `-overwrite`, `-fixed`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:control-bytes`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:test-path-roots` and `check:pending-changeset-literals`. `check:changeset-claims` is report-only. It named 7 pending changesets that cite `ListView.tsx`; I re-read each one and none is made false by this diff.

## Grading

This is defence in depth. ObjectStack's server strips denied fields from every returned row (`FieldMasker`), so nothing leaked from that backend. The projection matters for a backend that does not strip.

## Acceptance notes

- **Measured: what a predicate does when its operand is denied.** A denied operand is left out of the projection. The predicate then evaluates against an absent key. A one-shot `evalRowPredicate` probe (not committed) with `record.priority == 'low'` returned `true` for priority `low`, `false` for priority `high`, and the caller's fallback when `priority` was absent (`false` for fallback `false`, `true` for fallback `true`). `RowActionMenu` passes fallback `false` to both `visible` and `disabled`. So such an action is hidden when its `visible` operand is denied, and enabled when its `disabled` operand is denied. The same thing already happens on ObjectStack, where the masker removes the key, and on any partially-denied list. This PR does not change it.
- **Map view bindings are not projected.** Neither `locationField` nor `latitudeField` / `longitudeField` (flat, `map.*` or `options.map.*`) is in the builder's view-binding arm. A one-shot probe on this branch gave `$select` `['id', 'subject']` for columns `['subject']` with each spelling. `ObjectMap` draws from the host rows when `ListView` passes them. On a backend that honours `$select`, those rows arrive without the coordinates. The map's final render was read from source, not measured. This already happens today to every map view whose columns omit the location field. With this PR it also happens to a map view whose every column is denied. That view used to receive the whole record. It is reported to the seat as a separate finding, not fixed here.
- No doc describes `ListView`'s projection (the plugin-list README and `content/docs/guide` were read), so no doc changes.
